source: critic round 1 (counterpoint + musical lenses), 2026-09-24 23:40; the fixer that should have applied these was killed by the session limit

major_issues.issue: DESIGN-LEVEL. The apotheosis (51-58) is the thinnest-scored and most static passage in the piece, and the old flaw 1 (a first bar that is one static tonic chord) comes back at the most important moment. I scanned /Users/biobook/Music/llm-music/fugue-jp/ricercar/design/final-lab/SK_final.ly for four-voice beats with only one or two pitch classes: 9 of the 29 in the whole piece fall in bars 52-58. They are 52:1, 52:4, 53:1 (Bb2 F3 F4 Bb4), 54:4, 55:1 (F2 F3 F4 C5), 55:3, 56:3, 56:4 and 58:1. At 56:4 all four voices play F (F2 F3 F4 F5) on the tune's high f''. The synthesis log says the four-octave unisons were fixed at 13 and 17; the problem has moved to the peak of the tune. At 58:1 the chord is Bb2 C3 Bb4 C5: the plan calls it 'C7/B-flat', but there is no E and no G. The devices are also inaudible. The 'mirror of S1' in the bass (51-52) is a B-flat pedal with C neighbours, and 'answer against its own mirror' (bass f,2. f,8 e,8 against tenor f2. f8 g8) is an F octave pedal. At 58:4.5 the chord is F2 F3 G4 C5: the V before c''->d'' has no A and no E-flat. So the only authentic arrival on the major tonic (59:1) has no leading tone, and every other B-flat-major tonic is plagal (50->51) or over a pedal (61-62). Harmonically, 51-53 is the film's own I-IV6/4-I over a tonic pedal: the 'happy' sound the user objected to, not a transfiguration.
major_issues.fix: Replace the bass mirror in 51-54 with the exposition's proven order T5 moved into B-flat major, so the fugue's three subjects combine under the untouched tune. Soprano: the tune. Bass: CS1 (the lament) in major from 51:4: `bes,2. f,4 | d2. c4 | bes,4 a,4 aes,2 | ges,2. f,4 |`, eliding into the answer's f, at 55:1. Tenor: CS2 in major from 52:1: `bes8 a8 bes8 c'8 d'8 c'8 ees'8 g8 | d'4 c'8 f'8~ f'2 | ees'8 f'8 ees'8 d'8 c'4 d'4 |`, ending on the mirror's f at 55:1. I ran this as a 3-voice scratch lab (/tmp/critic/maj_lab.ly; no project file changed). ck.sh gives 0 errors, 0 PAR!, 0 BEAT, 0 DIS!; strict.py gives clash 0, xrel 0, acc 0, acc2 0; the only flags are T5's known tail D4?/DIR. The result is I | I6-ii7 | I-V6-v7/A-flat | iv6-I6/4 | V: a descending chromatic bass under a major tune, with the minor shadows (A-flat, G-flat) inside the major, an audible contrapuntal apotheosis instead of a film cue. The free alto still has to be added and checked. For 55-58: the alto (FREE) must carry the third A4 on 55:1, 56:3 and 56:4 (never F). Keep the tenor's mirror only where it is audible (57-58, contrary motion F-E-C against F-G-B-flat) and give the tenor A or E-flat in 55-56. Moving the mirror up an octave collides with the tune's f' at 55:3, so X9 alone is not proof. 58:1 needs E (alto) or E3/G3 (the tenor's landing note). 58:4.5 must be a full V7 (A and E-flat present) so that 58->59 is a real perfect cadence under c''->d''.

major_issues.issue: DESIGN-LEVEL. Climax II (46-49, the fff peak at 75% of the piece) is not earned by thematic content, and the crescendo runs on long notes. Attacks per bar in 46-49 are 9, 9, 7, 9, while the arioso's repeated chords (30-34) have 18-22; the shortest note in bar 49 is a quarter. So the surface rhythm slows as the dynamics rise. The only thematic lines are the tenor's S1 tail (mid-texture, Bb3-Eb4) and the bass augmentation in whole and half notes. The soprano holds F5 from 45:1 to 47:3 and then plays a free wedge; the blueprint itself calls the alto 'chord-filler'. The 'four forms at once' (44-45) come at p-mp, and three of the four (S1 bars 1-2, the INV head, INV augmented) are each one held note with a neighbour, so they will be heard as an F/B-flat drone under S2. Meanwhile the soprano's F5, a major second above the alto's S2 at 44:1 (theme bar 7), masks the tune's most recognisable bar (blueprint risk 10). The fff lands on F2 C4 C5 A5: the fifth doubled and the root only once. At 49:1 (C2 Bb3 E5 Bb5) the seventh is doubled and the fifth is missing. Climax I ends the same way: a crescendo to a fermata on an unstable chord, then silence and a subito pp.
major_issues.fix: (a) Adopt part4_variants x2 now: soprano silent until 46:3, and drop its 44:1-45:1 role from plan.json. Nothing audible is lost, and S2 is heard on top. (b) Make the wedge thematic and accelerating. Build 46:3-49:4 from S1 heads in diminution (x4. x16 (x-1)16: the piece's first sixteenths), rising by semitone, passed between soprano and alto in stretto at the half-bar. Keep the wedge's goal pitches (G-flat 47:4, G 48:3, B-flat 49:1, A 49:4) as the heads' main notes. This makes Climax II the mirror of Climax I's falling heads, and puts augmentation (bass) and diminution (upper voices) together, the Op. 110 / Contrapunctus 7 device the brief asks for. (c) At 49:4 double the root (alto F4 or F5 instead of C5); at 49:1 give one of the two B-flats to G. Prove it with a new lab next to X7 and with splice_check on sec06.

major_issues.issue: DESIGN-LEVEL. The tonal plan and pitch levels are monotonous, and the stretto opens by replaying entry 3. Bars 1-29 (about 99 s, 43% of the piece) never leave B-flat, F and E-flat minor; the first major-key area is the A-minor pivot at 34. Bar 21 is bar 10 beat for beat: bass S1 on B-flat2 again, with CS1 and CS2 swapped at the octave, so for two bars the listener hears entry 3 again before the soprano enters at 22. The Neapolitan C-flat at 23:3 repeats 12:3 at the same point of CS2 because the triple counterpoint is built that way, so the 'surprise' is heard twice. S1 is stated five times on B-flat (1, 9, 20, 44, 51). S2 is heard three times at the identical pitch c'' over F in the bass (30, 42, 55). The most recognisable half of the tune never travels.
major_issues.fix: Preferred: move the stretto pair (20-26) to the relative-major region. The leader goes to D-flat major (tenor on des or bass on des,) and the follower to G-flat major (soprano on ges'), a 4th above as now. The existing minor-dominant tails (24, 26) then sink back to B-flat minor for the i6/4 at 26:1 and the dim7 liquidation. That gives a false dawn that makes Climax I's collapse and the final major mean something; it is brief and in stretto, so not 'happy'. Retarget episode 18-19 to A-flat7 -> D-flat. It costs no time; re-prove X2 at the new level and the sec02/sec03 boundaries. Minimum fix if that is rejected: give the stretto leader to the tenor (or alto) at a new register, so that 20-21 is not bass S1 on B-flat2 again. Also treat S2's fixed c''-over-F as a design question: one S2 statement at another level, for example R1's subdominant pairing in the pedal section.

major_issues.issue: DESIGN-LEVEL. A minor, 'the large-scale lower neighbour', is never established as a key, so the B-flat, A, B-flat plan the concept rests on cannot be heard. The bass sits on E from 34:1 to 37:2 (about 14 s). A minor sounds only as a 6/4 (36) and a 6 chord (38:4). At 39:3, the INV's arrival on 1, the sonority is A3 A3 A4 E5: no third, and tenor and bass in unison. Tenor and bass meet again on F#3 at 39:4.5-40:1, so viola and cello collapse onto one pitch exactly where the inverted stretto ends. E minor gets a root-position tonic only on the weak eighth 40:4.5. Part III is two entries and a harmonic shunt: a passage, not the Op. 110 inverted fugue it is modelled on. check.py does not flag unisons, which is why X5 passed.
major_issues.fix: (a) Cheap and required: change the bass INV's final note at 39:3 from a4 to a,4 (A2; one landing note). Change the bass's free fis4 at 39:4 to b,4 to anticipate B7. Have the soprano (FREE 39-41) supply C5 at 39:3 (e.g. c''8 b'8 before the held d-sharp'', avoiding C->D-sharp). Then 39:3 is a complete root-position A-minor chord on the half-bar, the only real arrival of the neighbour key. (b) Better, if the budget allows: add a third INV entry (soprano, e'' or a'') one bar after the tenor, for about 2 extra bars. Pay for it by raising Part I from 74 to 78 (saves about 4.5 s over bars 1-27, and brings it closer to the film's 108, which helps recognition). Re-prove with a lab next to X5.

major_issues.issue: PIANO IDIOM (plan and score). Climax I's ff fermata is barely struck on the piano. At 29:1 only the soprano's C5 is a new attack. The bass E-flat2 was struck at 27:2.5, the tenor G-flat3 at 27:4.5 and the alto A4 at 28:2.5, all tied in. /Users/biobook/Music/llm-music/fugue-jp/ricercar/tools/perform.py sets piano loudness only at note-on, so the '< ff' of 26:3-28:4 is a crescendo on held strings, and the fermata chord (about 7 beats at 66) is mostly decayed sound under one fresh ff note. The same problem appears in the soprano's F5, tied from 46:1 to 47:3 during '< f' (the wedge's top is fading before its G-flat), and in the bass B-flat2, tied over 59-60 and 61-62 (about 17 s with the ritardando and fermata; sostenuto pedal does not refresh a decayed string).
major_issues.fix: Untie into 29:1 in all four voices (a'1, ges1 and ees,1 re-struck, same pitches, so no counterpoint changes) so that the fermata chord is attacked ff; on strings this becomes an equally good re-bowed ff chord. Re-attack f'' at 47:1, and bes, at 60:1 and 62:1. Alternatively, give perform.py a piano-target rule that re-strikes ties longer than one bar at the current dynamic level. Check every '<' in plan.json for spans where no voice attacks.

major_issues.issue: DESIGN-LEVEL. The minor-to-major hinge is one bar, and the apotheosis begins by deflating. After the fff V fermata at 49:4 and a 0.7 s breath, bar 50 (tempo 56, about 4.3 s, 7 attacks) goes IV -> iv6, and the tune enters at 51 at p, an octave below the soprano's stranded B-flat5. The nine-bar dominant pedal, the piece's longest tension, never resolves to I; it retrogresses V -> IV. The plagal / minor-iv colour appears three times in 12 bars (50 IV-iv6, 52:3 IV6/4 over I, 60 iv6/4), plus tonic pedals at 51-53 and 59-62. That is the 'Hollywood cadence' saturation that will read as film music, 'cheap' rather than transfigured.
major_issues.fix: Give the turn two bars, with the soprano descending by step from B-flat5 to the tune's B-flat4 (e.g. bes''4 aes''4 g''4 f''4 | ees''4 des''4 c''4 a'4 -> bes' at 51, checked against the chords). This connects the peak to the tune instead of dropping an octave. Consider making the first hinge chord bVI (G-flat major) rather than IV: the bass F -> G-flat is the INV's Phrygian neighbour at the largest scale, the fermata's A5 rises to B-flat5 as its third, and it is Beethoven's deceptive cadence rather than a V->IV retrogression. Then iv6 -> I. It costs about 4.3 s of the 12.7 s headroom (about 231.6 s). Inside 51-62 keep one minor-iv shadow, which the lament bass of issue 1 supplies naturally at 54:1, and not three.

minor_issues: Bars 33-34 are two whole bars of identical repeated eighth chords (V7, then E major) at tempo 52, about 9 s of chord padding (old flaw 2) at the plan's one big surprise. Add an inner suspension or moving line in 33, allowed by the sec04 spec, and let the bass or tenor move inside 34.

The arioso (30-34) is S2 stated plainly over pulsing chords for four bars. It has no dolente peak of its own, unlike Op. 110's arioso, and its 'one ray of light' at 31:4 sounds as D2 F3 F4 F5 (a bare D-F); B-flat arrives only on the next eighth. Voice 31:4 with the B-flat in the alto or tenor.

Violin II is below its compass at 9:4-13:3 (F3, G-flat3). The tenor (viola) rests in bars 9-12, so in the quartet render route the alto to the viola for those bars instead of pitch-stretching violin samples.

Same-pitch unisons merge voices at 5:3 (S=A on F4, the answer's entry swallowed by the subject's tail) and 15:2.5 (S=A on C5). Add a same-MIDI-pitch scan to splice_check.py; check.py does not report unisons.
At the bass entry 9:1-9:2.5 the chord is E5 G4 Bb2: a diminished triad until C arrives at 9:3. The blueprint's 'C7/B-flat' is not what is heard for the first two beats.

Entry 4 (13-17) is the first four-voice moment, but the soprano descant is whole and half notes separated by rests, with a hollow 13:3 (F2 F3 A3 F5) and 17:3 (C2 C3 C5 E5). This is where 'shallow' will be heard. The sec02 composer should treat it as the main task, not optional (blueprint risk 8 understates it).

Two climaxes with the same gesture: a crescendo to a fermata on a dim7 or V over a pedal, then silence or a breath, then subito pp (29->30, 49->50), plus a third subito at 42. By the second time it is predictable. Vary one: for example, Climax I breaks off without a fermata, or Climax II resolves through the bVI hinge in major issue 6.

The apotheosis dynamics are misaligned: f is reached at 57:1 and already falls toward mp from 57:3, while the melodic peak (the f'' at 56:4) is the four-octave unison. Place the f on 56:4-57:2 and fix the voicing first.
Hollow beats inside the Climax II crescendo: 46:3 is F2 C4 C5 F5.

The coda (59-62) has 20 attacks in 4 bars over a 4-bar tonic pedal, and the soprano's d'' (the 'question answered') sits for 8 beats with nothing moving. If major issue 1's lament bass is not adopted, put CS1's chromatic tetrachord in the alto under the held d'' (59: bes' a' aes' g' -> 60: ges' f', which is already written), ending on the existing iv6/4.

The blueprint's '54% chromatic attacks' from harmony.py does not show harmonic surprise. It counts raised leading tones, and the tool's labels in 9-12 ('#ii2', etc.) suggest the key mapping is inflating it. The real harmonic events are few: Neapolitan x3 (two of them the same CS2 spot), the dim7 slide, the German-sixth pivot, V7/V at 48 and the V->IV at 49-50. Don't cite the metric as proof of depth.

At 13:1 the upper staff (S+A) spans F5 to A3. The pianist can take A3 in the left hand (C3 F3 A3), but the print distribution should be decided now, because the blueprint's spans are wide in 13-19, 21-29, 42-50 and 53-56.

The lab X9 ('answer against its own mirror') and the claim 'tune over its own mirror' are true on paper but inaudible in their first two bars, because the head is a repeated note: a mirror of a pedal is a pedal. Describe them honestly in the notes, or use them where their moving bars (3-5) coincide with other moving lines.

major_issues.issue: Climax I, the liquidation at 26:3-29, never sounds the E diminished seventh it claims, so §0(4) ('the neighbour applied to a whole chord'), the §4 form table, §4.3 and the §6 section-3 harmony line are all false. Each head slides to its semitone 3.5 beats after it enters. The entries are only 2 beats apart, so every voice has already slid before the next head arrives. The grid shows what actually sounds: 26:3 E-Bb-G (triad); 27:1-27:2.5 E2 G3 G4 only (two pitch classes, three voices, during the crescendo to ff); 27:2.5 the bass is already on E-flat; 27:3 E-flat major; 27:4.5 e-flat minor; 28:1 E-flat Gb Bb Db (e-flat minor 7, when the D-flat finally enters); 28:4.5 A dim7 over E-flat. The E and the D-flat are never heard together. The 'glimpse of light' E-flat major at 27:3 is a side effect of the staggering, explained after the fact.
major_issues.fix: Hold each head's first note until all four are sounding, then slide the whole chord together. Bass 26-29: f,2 e,2~ | e,1~ | e,2. e,8 ees,8~ | ees,1. Tenor: bes1 | g1~ | g2. g8 ges8~ | ges1. Alto: bes'2 g'2~ | g'2 bes'2~ | bes'2. bes'8 a'8~ | a'1. Soprano unchanged. Result: the full E dim7 (E2 G3 Bb4 Db5) sounds 28:1-28:4.5 at ff, then all four voices drop a semitone at 28:4.5 into A dim7 over E-flat. No perfect intervals move in parallel. Tested: check.py 0 errors/0 PAR!/0 BEAT/0 DIS! on the whole piece; strict.py clash 0, xrel 0 in 26-29; duration still 227.3 s. Then regenerate the section-3 boundary table (A, T and B last notes now start at 28:4.5) and proofs.txt. If the staggered version is kept, rewrite all four claims to describe what actually sounds.

major_issues.issue: The 'combination of subjects' (the fix claimed for old flaw 4) is nominal. S2 (alto 42) and S1 (tenor 44) overlap for only 8 beats (S2's bars 3-4 over S1's bars 1-2), and one of those bars is S2's held c''1, so there is one bar of real two-subject counterpoint. The 'four thematic forms at once' (§1, §10.4) counts a 3-note INV head (f'' f'' ges'') that just doubles the pedal's F/G-flat. The only full-length S1+S2 combination (R1) is shelved as 'not planned'.
major_issues.fix: Bring S2 in with S1 at 44:1. Alto 42-43: r1 | r1, leaving bass pedal + tenor lament lead-in, a genuinely misterioso two-voice start. Alto 44-47: c''4. a'8 f'4 des''8 bes'8 | c''2. f''8 bes'8 | ees''4. des''8 des''4. c''8 | c''1. Alto 48-50 unchanged. Soprano 44-46 = variant x2: r1 | r1 | r2 f''2~. Tested on the whole piece: check.py 0/0/0/0, strict clash 0 (the old D4? at 47:1 disappears), 227.3 s. This gives the two halves of the tune together, complete, over the augmented inversion for 16 beats, at no time cost. Keeping the soprano INV head with S2 at 44 also passes, but puts S2's F5 in unison with the soprano at 45:4 and makes A-Bb-Gb clusters at 44:4.5 and 45:4.5, so use x2. Update plan.json (alto subject 44:1-48:1; delete soprano 44:1-45:1), the section-6 spec (47:4 ii°7 loses its E-flat; alto boundary now starts with a rest) and §0, §4 and §10.

major_issues.issue: Bar 20, the first bar of the stretto leader, repeats old flaw 1 exactly. After beat 1 the tenor and soprano rest, so for three beats the bass S1 head (Bb2) sits under the alto's held F4: a bare open fifth, one static tonic, no third. The tenor rest at 20:2-4 is not declared FREE (section 3 lists only S 20:1, T 24-26, A 25-27:2, B 25-26:2), so no composer is allowed to fix it. The §2.1 claim 'every accompanied statement harmonises bar 1 twice' is also false for bar 5: entry 2's first bar is a single F-major arpeggio in two voices, with the S1 tail landing in unison on F4 at 5:3.
major_issues.fix: Declare tenor 20:2-20:4 FREE and require at least two harmonies in bar 20. Tested example: tenor bar 20 = bes4 des'4 ees'4 c'4. It gives i, i, i with a suspended 4th (E-flat over B-flat), then F/A = V6 at 20:4.5 over the bass's A2, and steps into CS2 at 21:1. Whole piece still 0/0/0/0, strict clash 0. Correct §2.1 so the claim covers only entries 3, 4 and 22.

major_issues.issue: The episode instruction in section 2(b) cannot be executed as written, and its label is wrong. The alto 'mirror' ges'4. f'8 f'4. ees'8 is not a mirror of cell b: it is the soprano's own bar 19 (ges''4. f''8 f''4. ees''8) an octave lower. Tested placements: in bar 19 it gives PAR! S/A octaves at 19:1->19:2.5 and 19:3->19:4.5 plus BEAT octaves 19:2->19:3; in bar 18 it gives an augmented-fourth leap C5->Gb4 plus BEAT fifths A/B at 18:4->19:1. No bar or beat is specified.
major_issues.fix: Replace the text with a proven line and a location. Tested: alto 18-19 = aes'2 bes'4. a'8 | a'4. c''8 a'2. This answers cell b's rhythm at the half bar, keeps the A4 boundary at 19:3, and gives check.py 0/0/0/0 and strict clash 0. Otherwise require any suggested imitation to state bar, beat and pitch and to pass splice_check before it goes into the spec.

major_issues.issue: The plan's logic is not enforced for parallel composers. splice_check reports changed countersubject notes only as WARN, so the triple-counterpoint identity (the core of §2.4) can be rewritten and still PASS. None of the 'FREE but keep' items are checked at all: the soprano c''2 b'2 pivot at 34, the tenor lament lead-in at 42-43, the wedge pitches at 45-50, the IV6/4 at 52:3, the alto E natural at 56:1, the soprano d'' at 59, and the alto G-flat to F at 60. One declared freedom is also impossible: section 6 says 'T 49-50 FREE', but the tenor's bes2~ starting at 48:3 falls inside the S1 lock span (44:1-48:4). splice_check compares note start and duration, so any change to 49:1-49:3 returns LOCK FAIL.
major_issues.fix: In splice_check.py, make countersubject changes FAIL except inside an explicit landing window per countersubject span (add 'landing_from' to the cs roles in plan.json). Add a role 'keep' that is checked like LOCK for the items listed above. For the tenor tie at 48:3-49:3, either split the tie in the skeleton (bes2 | bes2. c'4) or change the section-6 text to 'T 49:4-50 FREE'.

minor_issues: INV stretto collision (both spans LOCKED, so no composer can fix it): the bass INV's final tonic A3 at 39:3 is in unison with the tenor INV's A3, and the free bass F#3 at 39:4 doubles the tenor's F#3 at 39:4.5. The end of the first inverted entry disappears into the second, and on piano the same key is struck twice. Fix: bass 39 = d4. f8 a,4 fis,4. Tested: 0/0/0/0, no unisons remain.

Harmony labels that composers are told to 'keep' do not match the notes. 43:4 'vii°4/2' is only Gb2 Gb3 F5 (a neighbour note). 37:1 'VI' is E3 B3 E4 C5, with a minor 9th C5 against B3 on the tenor's INV entry. 36 'i6/4' has no A. 22:2.5 'v7 (F minor 7)' has the alto's A natural. 58:1 'C7/B-flat' has no E. 58:4 'V6' is the quartal sonority A2 D3 G4 C5, where both thematic neighbours are flagged ESC?. 39:4-40 'suspension' D#5 is a chord tone of B7. Re-derive the labels from a grid.
'IV (E-flat major, the first G natural)' at 50 is false: the same E-flat major chord (G3) already sounds at 27:3, and G naturals occur at 7, 15, 17, 27 and 48.
'F2 is a nine-bar pedal' and 'double pedal F2/F5 44-47': the bass leaves F at 46:4 (then E-flat, C, D-flat, F, E-flat, G-flat). The pedal is 42:1-46:3 and the double pedal 44:1-46:3.

The checker is lenient in ways that matter for the 0 DIS! claims. It passes a dissonance if either voice has any label, so strong-beat dissonances are 'justified' by the motion of the consonant voice (26:3 B-flat over E2 as B:ANT; 44:1-45:3 the tenor's B-flat a 4th over the pedal as B:ANT/B:RET; 13:1 and 17:2.5 6/4s as B:ESC?). It measures intervals in semitones, so spelled dissonances are invisible to check.py, and strict.py flags only augmented unisons and octaves. Examples: 60:1-60:3 soprano D5 held against G-flat 4 (augmented 5th) and E-flat 4 (e-flat minor with a major 7th over the B-flat pedal, not a clean iv6/4); 34:1-34:3 C5 against G#3 (diminished 4th). Confirm these by ear and say so in the blueprint.

suspensions.py over-counts: it credits held chord tones (33:3 bass F2 under V7; 40:3 alto A4, the 7th of B7) and never checks the preparation, so the '12 suspensions, target 30' metric can be met without real suspensions.

Risk 3's suggestion to give alto 9:4-13:3 to the viola cannot work: the viola (tenor) starts the answer at 13:1 while the CS1 tail runs to 13:3. Give the viola 9:4-12:4 only; violin II takes the tail from 13:1 (A3 is in range).

Unisons between adjacent voices: 5:3 S/A F4 (the soprano's S1 ending is swallowed by the alto's held F4) and 15:2.5 S/A C5 (the free descant doubles CS2). Voice overlap at 57:1: the alto's C5 sits above the tune's previous B-flat 4.

Keyboard spans are worse than risk 4 says. The lower staff (T+B) exceeds a 10th in 20 of 62 bars (13, 15, 16, 19, 21, 22, 24-26, 30, 42, 44-49, 53, 54, 60; widest 25 semitones). The upper staff exceeds a 10th in bars 11-13, 36 and 50 (widest 23). The alto-tenor gap is more than an octave throughout 42-50, leaving a hole in the middle of Climax II.

The tenor lament lead-in's last note G-flat 3 (43:4) doubles the bass's G-flat 2 and leaps up to B-flat 3 instead of resolving. At 48:3-49:4 the 7th of C7 is doubled (tenor B-flat 3 and soprano B-flat 5), and the tenor's copy rises to C4. Acceptable in free style, but not strict.
In 42:4.5 the alto's B-flat 4 (S2) sounds against the tenor's A3, the note the tenor's 4-3 suspension has just resolved to.
Global rule 5 ('no chordal padding') contradicts section 4, whose accompaniment is pulsing repeated-eighth chords. Say that section 4 is exempt (Op. 110 arioso model).
plan.json gives the alto's CS1 first note f'1 at 20:1 no role, so perform.py plays it as a free voice (-4). The soprano cs role runs to 39:4 although the spec declares S 39-41 FREE.
CS1 is called 'the chromatic fourth of Bach's Thema Regium', but D-flat C B-flat A A-flat G-flat F spans a minor sixth and contains two whole steps. Only D-flat-C and B-flat-A-A-flat are chromatic.
Head treatment is inconsistent: the tenor re-attacks G-flat 3 at 28:1 and the soprano re-attacks C5 at 29:1, while bass and alto tie. Choose one on purpose; this matters for the strings.

Duration arithmetic, entry lengths (S1 19 beats, S2 16, INV augmentation 38 = exactly 2x, elided at 51), the real answer, the INV, mirror and answer-mirror mappings, and 'entry 4 = T4 down a perfect fourth' all verified correct. Re-measured 227.3 s (piano and strings); all 7 starters PASS splice_check; SK_final compiles.
